# <span id="aanchor167"></span> Master Allocation Setup

[&lt;&lt; Back](Master%20Allocation%20-%20Setup.md) \| <a href="#" class="selected">Gas Allocation</a> \| [Liquid Allocation](Master%20Allocation%20-%20Setup%20-%20Liquid.md)

## Gas Allocation

<div class="procedure">

To set up a master meter (gas):

1.  Go to **Tools** \> **Master Allocation** \> **Setup**.

2.  Click the **Gas** radio button.

3.  Click **New**.

4.  Select a gas meter to become the master meter.

5.  Select a direction for the master meter.

6.  Set the energy allocation method.

7.  Select the date range for the allocation.

8.  Use the Available Meters list to locate meters to include in the allocation. Double-click a meter to move it to the Meter Members list, or select multiple meters and click the right arrow button.

    Outlet meters are highlighted in blue; inlet meters are highlighted in red.

9.  Indicate the meters that you want to <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCTextPopup MCTextPopupHotSpot MCTextPopup_Open glossaryTerm MCTextPopupHotSpot_" alt="Closed" data-mc-alt2="Open">keep whole<span class="MCTextPopupBody popupBody"><span class="MCTextPopupArrow"></span>Volume, energy, and mass for meters that are "kept whole" in the allocation process will not be adjusted to compensate for a surplus or deficit.</span></a> during the allocation process.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 558;height: 440;" />

If a direction has not been defined for a meter in Meter Characteristics, you will be prompted to select a direction. Meters without an assigned direction will be highlighted with a red and white border.

</div>

#### Gas Calculation Method

When calculating allocation values for a master meter, the balance arithmetic used is based on the base direction of the master.

For master meters with an inlet base direction:

<span style="color: #ff0000;">Inlet Meter </span>= <span style="color: #ff0000;">Inlet Meters </span>– <span style="color: #4169e1;">Outlet Meters</span>

For master meters with an outlet base direction:

<span style="color: #4169e1;">Outlet Meter</span> = <span style="color: #4169e1;">Outlet Meters </span>– <span style="color: #ff0000;">Inlet Meters</span>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example 1">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example 1 - Gas Allocation</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example 1">

A master meter has three meter members (Meter 1 \[<span style="color: #ff0000;">inlet</span>\], Meter 2 \[<span style="color: #4169e1;">outlet</span>\], and Meter 3 \[<span style="color: #4169e1;">outlet</span>\]).

The master meter has direction set to outlet, so the following balance arithmetic will be used:

<span style="color: #4169e1;">Outlet Meter </span>= <span style="color: #4169e1;">Outlet Meters </span>– <span style="color: #ff0000;">Inlet Meters</span>



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 417;height: 338;" />

For Volume:

The master total volume differs from the member total volume.

Difference = Master Total Volume – Member Total Volume

300 - 245 = 55

This difference must be allocated proportionally across member meters.

Allocation = Difference \* (Individual Meter / Member Total)

> | Meter |            Allocation            |
> |:-----:|:--------------------------------:|
> |   1   | 55 \* (-360 / 245) = **- 80.82** |
> |   2   |  55 \* (195 / 245) = **43.78**   |
> |   3   |  55 \* (410 / 245) = **92.04**   |

The allocation will then be added to each member’s volume to create a revised allocated volume per meter.

> | Meter | Original Volume | Allocation | Revised Volume |
> |:-----:|:---------------:|:----------:|:--------------:|
> |   1   |      -360       |   -80.82   |    -440.82     |
> |   2   |       195       |   43.78    |     238.78     |
> |   3   |       410       |   92.04    |     502.04     |
> | Total |       245       |    N/A     |      300       |

The revised member total volume now equals the master total volume.

Energy and mass are allocated in the same manner. This may cause a disconnect between the meter’s heating value and the energy/volume ratio and/or energy/mass ratio.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example 2">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example 2 - Gas Allocation with Keep Whole</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example 2">

A master meter has three meter members (Meter 1 \[<span style="color: #ff0000;">inlet</span>\], Meter 2 \[<span style="color: #4169e1;">outlet</span>\], and Meter 3 \[<span style="color: #4169e1;">outlet</span>\]).

The master meter has direction set to outlet, so the following balance arithmetic will be used:

<span style="color: #4169e1;">Outlet Meter </span>= <span style="color: #4169e1;">Outlet Meters </span>– <span style="color: #ff0000;">Inlet Meters</span>



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 417;height: 338;" />

Meter 2 will be "kept whole", indicating that the volume, energy, and mass for that meter will not be adjusted to compensate for a surplus or deficit.

For Volume:

The volume of the kept whole meter will be subtracted from the master total to create a new master total for allocation.

New Master Total Volume = Master Total Volume - Kept Whole Volume

300 - 195 = 105

The total volume for the three member meters is 245. The volume of the kept whole meter will be subtracted from the total volume of the meter members to create a new member total volume.

New Member Total Volume = Member Total Volume - Kept Whole Volume

245 - 155 = 50

The new master total volume differs from the new member total volume.

Difference = New Master Total Volume – New Member Total Volume

105 - 50 = 55

This difference must be allocated proportionally across the two member meters that are not being kept whole.

Allocation = Difference \* (Individual Meter / Member Total)

> | Meter |          Allocation          |
> |:-----:|:----------------------------:|
> |   1   | 55 \* (-360 / 50) = **-396** |
> |   2   |       N/A (kept whole)       |
> |   3   |  55 \* (410 / 50) = **451**  |

The allocation will then be added to each member’s volume to create a revised allocated volume per meter.

> | Meter | Original Volume | Allocation | Revised Volume |
> |:-----:|:---------------:|:----------:|:--------------:|
> |   1   |      -360       |    -396    |      -756      |
> |   2   |       195       |     0      |      195       |
> |   3   |       410       |    451     |      861       |
> | Total |       245       |    N/A     |      300       |

The revised member total volume now equals the master total.

Energy and mass are allocated in the same manner. This may cause a disconnect between the meter’s heating value and the energy/volume ratio and/or energy/mass ratio.

</div>
